messages:
Allison Grant: starting a thread for Runtime Profiles dashboard planning. need to lock metric names + labels this week so i can hand off a spec to obs-pack.

Allison Grant: main use cases i’m optimizing for:
1) “profile adoption” — what % of traffic is on profile_pack enabled + which profile_id/profile_version
2) perf compare — p95/p99 latency + tokens/sec broken down by sku + profile_id
3) safety — kernel fallback spikes, scheduler queueing, OOM/frag signals

Caleb Johnson: +1. pls be super careful w/ label cardinality. if we label latency histos with `model_id` + `customer_id` + `route` + `profile_id` we’re gonna melt Mimir.

Omar El-Sayed: runtime side we already tagged some histos w/ `sku` and will add `profile_id` / `profile_version` in ENG-4931. question is how much do we include on the “hot path” metrics.

Julian Moore: scheduler metrics i’m adding:
- `scheduler_queue_ms` (hist)
- `scheduler_inflight_requests` (gauge)
- `scheduler_bucket` (string-ish label but low cardinality: `short`, `mixed`, `long`)

Julian Moore: please don’t make me add `prompt_len` as a label 😅

Allison Grant: agreed. proposal: metric labels limited to:
- `cluster` / `region` (existing)
- `sku` (H100/L40S/B200)
- `profile_id` (like `h100-balanced-v1`)
- `profile_version` (pack version e.g. `1.0.0`)
- `deployment_mode` (hosted/dedicated/private) if already standard

Allison Grant: explicitly *not* adding `customer_id`, `model_name`, `route` to the base histos. we can get those via tracing / logs.

Caleb Johnson: 👍 this matches our current label budget.

Ethan Park: from control plane side we can also emit a separate low-frequency “inventory” metric per pool: active profile_version + sku + instance_type. might help adoption w/o touching request metrics.

Allison Grant: nice. for adoption we can do it two ways:
A) from request metrics: % of requests by `profile_id/profile_version`
B) from inventory: how many nodes/pools on each profile_version

Rafael Mendes: from SRE POV we care about A more than B during rollout. if only 10% of nodes are canary but they’re handling 50% of traffic (hot shard) we need to see that.

Sofia Ivanova: for scheduler changes, adoption panel should include “pack enabled” yes/no. we’ll be doing feature-flag on some pools.

Allison Grant: good call. should we add `profile_pack_enabled` label (boolean) OR encode as `profile_id=legacy` when off?

Caleb Johnson: please do NOT add boolean labels to every metric (sounds harmless but it doubles series). better to set `profile_id="legacy"` and `profile_version="0"` when pack disabled.

Omar El-Sayed: we can do that. runtime already has “no profile” path; we can set:
- `profile_id=legacy-default`
- `profile_version=0.0.0`

Allison Grant: perfect.

Allison Grant: metric names — keeping consistent w/ our conventions:
- `redwood_runtime_request_latency_ms` (hist)
- `redwood_runtime_decode_toks_per_s` (hist or summary?)
- `redwood_runtime_prefill_ms` (hist)
- `redwood_runtime_decode_ms` (hist)
- `redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_ms` (hist)
- `redwood_runtime_kernel_fallback_total` (counter)
- `redwood_runtime_oom_total` (counter)
- `redwood_runtime_kv_compaction_ms` (hist)
- `redwood_runtime_fragmentation_estimate` (gauge)

Caleb Johnson: hist for latency breakdowns is good. for toks/sec, avoid a label-per-model. simplest is `tokens_generated_total` + `request_decode_seconds_total` and compute rate. but if runtime is already exporting `decode_toks_per_s` as hist it’s ok.

Julian Moore: trace side already has stage spans (`queue`, `prefill`, `decode`). could we use exemplars to link p99 spikes -> traces?

Caleb Johnson: we can, but only if we keep the label set small (which we are). exemplars get dropped when series explode.

Allison Grant: ok.

Allison Grant: cardinality risk areas i see:
- `profile_id` can grow if we let everyone create custom profile ids
- `profile_version` increments each release

Allison Grant: mitigation i’m thinking:
1) `profile_id` must be from the shipped pack only (no free-form), customer overrides are *pins* not custom ids
2) `profile_version` stays semver-ish but capped in retention (dash shows last ~10 versions)

Ethan Park: we can enforce (1) in control plane (override schema). runtime also should refuse unknown profile_id unless `allow_unsafe_overrides=true` in private.

Omar El-Sayed: yep, PR-24944 has guardrails. in Private we’ll allow custom but we can set label to `profile_id=custom` and log the actual id to avoid cardinality.

Caleb Johnson: that’s the right pattern.

Allison Grant: cool. dashboard mockups (rough):

Allison Grant: Panel group 1 — Adoption
- Stacked area: `rate(request_total[5m])` by `profile_id` (filtered by sku)
- Table: top profiles by traffic + p95 latency delta vs baseline (needs baseline selector)
- Stat: % traffic on `profile_version != 0.0.0`

Allison Grant: Panel group 2 — Perf
- p95/p99 `request_latency_ms` by `profile_id` (split by sku)
- p95 `scheduler_queue_ms` by `profile_id`
- Heatmap: queue_ms vs time for canary clusters

Allison Grant: Panel group 3 — Safety signals
- kernel fallback rate: `rate(kernel_fallback_total[5m])` by `fallback_reason`
- OOM rate: `rate(oom_total[5m])` by sku
- kv compaction p95 + fragmentation gauge

Rafael Mendes: can we add a panel for “profile mismatch” incidents? like when model reload crosses pool and picks wrong profile (PR-24958 fix). we need a counter.

Omar El-Sayed: good call — i can add `redwood_runtime_profile_mismatch_total` (counter). labels: sku + profile_id only.

Caleb Johnson: 👍 keep reason label low-cardinality if needed: `reason=model_reload|config_drift`.

Sofia Ivanova: for scheduler, would love a panel: “% time spent queueing” = queue_ms / (queue+compute). should be easy from histos.

Allison Grant: yep. we can do ratio from p50 or from avg; ratio of p95s is a bit misleading but still useful for “is queueing dominating” alerts.

Caleb Johnson: fyi ratio-of-percentiles is not mathematically sound but good enough as a heuristic. just label it as heuristic.

Allison Grant: ack.

Allison Grant: open question: do we tag latency w/ `kernel_choice`? would be nice for debugging but feels high-cardinality.

Omar El-Sayed: kernel_choice is small set (v1/v2/v3/fallback) but it multiplies series on the biggest histo. i’d rather export `kernel_choice_total{choice=...}` as a counter and keep latency histo clean.

Caleb Johnson: +1. separate counter is best.

Allison Grant: ok.

Slackbot: Reminder: don’t forget to update the runbook links once the dashboard UID is created.

Allison Grant: action items:
- @Allison Grant: write dashboard + alert spec doc + send to obs-pack PR owner (today)
- @Caleb Johnson: confirm label budget + any reserved label names we shouldn’t use (today)
- @Omar El-Sayed: add `profile_mismatch_total` + confirm legacy labeling plan (`profile_id=legacy-default`) (this week)
- @Ethan Park: propose inventory metric shape for pool/node adoption (this week)

Caleb Johnson: will do. also pls use `profile_version` not `pack_version` as the label so it matches runtime config field.

Omar El-Sayed: 👍

Rafael Mendes: once we have the panels, SRE wants an alert: kernel fallback rate > X for 10m AND p95 latency delta > Y vs baseline. (avoid paging on expected low-level fallbacks).

Allison Grant: makes sense. will capture as “composite page” vs “ticket only” in alert spec.

Julian Moore: can you add a panel that shows `scheduler_bucket` distribution by profile? i want to see if bucketization is stable during canary.

Allison Grant: yep. stacked bar: `rate(request_total[5m])` by `scheduler_bucket` filtered to canary cluster.

Allison Grant: i’ll post a link to the draft spec once it’s in confluence.

Caleb Johnson: thanks. and pls keep `deployment_mode` out unless we’re sure it’s already a standard label on these metrics. otherwise it’s another multiplier.

Allison Grant: fair. i’ll list it as “optional if already present; do not add just for this project”.

Omar El-Sayed: for Dedicated we might still want to filter. but can rely on existing `cluster` naming or `tenant_tier`? (whatever we have today)

Caleb Johnson: exactly. don’t invent a new label in runtime for this.

Allison Grant: ok closing loop. will post draft spec + mock panels later today.
